ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When water flows out of the tubule of the descending limb of the loop of Henle, what type of transport occurs?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the structure of the loop of Henle; on the left is the descending limb (Descending limb), and beside it there are multiple arrows labeled “Water flow,” indicating that water flows outward from the lumen of the descending limb to the surrounding hypertonic medulla (osmotic medulla). Beside the ascending limb (Ascending limb) on the right is labeled “Ions actively pumped,” indicating that active pumping out of ions occurs in the ascending limb. Then reason: The question asks about the type of transport when water flows out of the tubule of the descending limb of the loop of Henle. Water moves passively along the osmotic gradient and does not consume ATP; if it moves through membrane channels such as aquaporins, in the classification of the options it belongs to channel-mediated passive transport, that is, facilitated diffusion. Active transport corresponds to the pumping out of ions in the ascending limb in the figure, not the outflow of water from the descending limb.
